description: Pins the NTV8 vault.meta generation: the NTV6 tail byte for byte with NO person wrap, so the master password is the only vault credential and the identity phrase opens nothing. Length is 445 + roster_len with any other length invalid, which is what makes the absence structural rather than a zeroed block a later writer could relax. Also pins the NTV7 to NTV8 upgrade, which is a truncation and re-wraps no key: the password a user already has still opens the file, and `upgrade-from-ntv7` carries that as one case (expected bytes AND the root_key they open to). `parse_fail` cases are expected to return the one non-distinguishing invalid-metadata result. Generated by `cargo test -p protocol --lib emit_vault_meta_ntv8_vectors_for_paste -- --ignored --nocapture`.

cases.description: A full NTV8 frame as creation writes it: the 345-byte base with its three phrase-wrap fields zero and root_key sealed under the password, then the NTV6 tail (owner-wrapped group key, epoch 1, sealed roster) and nothing after the roster. parse then re-serialize must reproduce these bytes exactly, and every field must be read back at its offset.

The frame above, opened with its master password alone: Argon2id over the 'myne.v0.2 argon2id-password|' salt domain with the frame's own KDF parameters and account_number_hash, then AEAD-open of enc_root_key_password under the 'password-wrap' role bound to those parameters. This is the case that fails when a port's salt domain, AAD role or 11-byte KDF block drifts while it parses every field correctly.

The same frame with a one-character-longer password. The refusal is the ONE non-distinguishing AEAD failure: a port must not report 'wrong password' in a way that distinguishes it from a tampered frame.
cases.informational_reason: a different password derives a different wrap key

cases.description: An NTV7 frame and what it must become on the first unlock under NTV8: the same bytes with the 1208-byte person envelope removed and the magic rewritten to NTV8. Nothing else moves, and no key is re-wrapped, which is why the SAME password opens the upgraded frame to the SAME root_key. A port that re-derives or re-wraps anything produces different bytes here, and a port that re-wraps the root key produces a frame this password no longer opens.

A whole, valid NTV7 frame fed to an NTV8 reader: base and tail are byte-identical, so the ONLY things distinguishing the two generations are the magic and the 1208 bytes after the roster. A lenient reader would accept this and then wait for a person wrap credential the user no longer has; the length rule is what makes that impossible.
The same frame with its magic relabelled NTV6. The tail is byte-identical to NTV6's, so this is the case that holds a reader to the magic rather than to the layout.
The same frame with its magic relabelled NTV7, which differs only in that it would demand 1208 more bytes. A reader keyed on the tail layout alone cannot tell the two apart.

A byte written into the recovery SALT (offset 49). NTV8 retires the phrase wrap, so a frame carrying any byte of it is structurally invalid rather than a vault whose saved phrase may or may not still work.
A byte written into the recovery wrap NONCE (offset 153). Same structural rule as the salt.
A byte written into the recovery-wrapped root_key (offset 177). The third and last field the phrase wrap occupied.
One byte appended after the roster. The frame length is fixed at 445 + roster_len, so trailing bytes are a rejection and not an extension point.
group_key_epoch forced to 0 (bytes 433..441). An epoch of zero is not a valid group-key generation in any NTV6-derived frame.
